title: The strict zero-harmonic Maxwell sector is not invariant for generic Gauss-compatible data

regeneration.averaged_maxwell_equation: On normalized T3, spatially averaging Maxwell gives partial_t E_h=-bar(j), up to the fixed sign convention; Gauss constrains div E and total charge but not E_h
regeneration.explicit_data: Choose A=0, E=0, phi=a exp(i k dot x)v_q, pi=0 with q nonzero and k nonzero. The charge density is zero, so Gauss holds, while bar(j)=e q |a|^2 k is nonzero
regeneration.consequence: Although E_h(0)=0, partial_t E_h(0) is nonzero. The strict zero-harmonic sector therefore leaves itself immediately for this smooth finite-mode datum
regeneration.relation_to_k1442: K1442 remains correct for an externally restricted p!=0 phase. The new result says that restriction is not a generic invariant reduction of the nonlinear PDE
regeneration.surviving_scope: Special symmetry sectors forcing bar(j)=0 may be invariant and remain open, but they are nongeneric additional hypotheses
